This occurs when an attacker can log in without knowing any password, and can do so by sending a very long password (257 to 1024 bytes) to the SSH port. This is possible if the system has an account whose password field is an empty string, or if the system has a key-only user created without a password. The vulnerability affects all Alpine Linux releases from 3.21 through 3.24 and edge, and older releases that no longer receive regular updates.

articles.title: sshole

This was changed in the 1990s with the introduction of the Unix password hash, which uses a salt to prevent rainbow table attacks.
